# dictionaries

**A local dictionary server with an English dictionary, a thesaurus, computing terms and acronyms**

- **Version recorded:** 1.13.1
- **Categories:** `references`
- **Upstream:** <https://sourceforge.net/projects/dict/>

## What it does

Runs dictd, a dictionary server, with four databases: GCIDE (a large English dictionary descended from Webster's 1913), WordNet (definitions and synonyms), FOLDOC (computing terms) and VERA (acronyms). `dict WORD` looks a word up in all of them from a terminal; goldendict-ng does the same on the desktop.

## Why you would want it

A word, a synonym or an acronym, answered with no network, in 32 MB rather than the 9 GB of an offline Wiktionary. Acronyms especially: a message passed on a net is full of them.

## Before it will work

Nothing. dictd starts as a system service when installed and listens on 127.0.0.1 port 2628 only.

## How it installs

- apt: `dictd`, `dict`, `dict-gcide`, `dict-wn`, `dict-foldoc`, `dict-vera`

## Known problems

dictd listens on loopback because Debian's shipped configuration says so; if you edit /etc/dictd/dictd.conf to share it, you are opening a server to the network. `dict -D` lists the databases. Translation dictionaries are separate `dict-freedict-*` packages (253 of them in Debian, 32 from English) and are not installed here: choose the ones for the languages you serve.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade

## Where to get help with the software itself

The DICT development group (https://dict.org/); the Debian packages' bug trackers for packaging problems.
